   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688

| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Critical

OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 15 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Vietnam-aligned threat actor known as OceanLotus has been attributed to two distinct campaigns that targeted domestic entities and stock investors with a backdoor known as SPECTRALVIPER. The campaigns involve a prolonged cyber espionage operation aimed at a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation between mid-2024 and February 2026, as well as a supply chain attack

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit.exe spawning setup.exe — malicious update download chain · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load — DtlCrashCatch.dll dropped/loaded from non-system path · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 IOC sightings — file write, process exec, image load · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus / SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure callouts · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

FireAnt Metakit.exe spawning setup.exe — malicious update download chain AIDelivery High
Hunts the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain entry point where the legitimate Metakit.exe (the FireAnt stock-investor client) launches a tampered setup.exe pulled from the unsigned update server. ESET notes the version.xml at metakit.fireant.vn lacks integrity validation, so the legit client process becomes the parent of the OceanLotus downloader. Rationale: Pivot is the article-specific parent binary 'Metakit.exe' (FireAnt's client) — there is no legitimate reason for it to spawn a setup.exe out of a user-writable directory. Cross-checked with ESET's report and Elastic Security Labs' 2023 SPECTRALVIPER write-up which describes the same DLL side-loading pattern via 'legitimate' parent binaries (https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper). Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt update after they finally implement signing (would still be unusual today)
  • FireAnt installer re-run by sysadmin during reimage to %Public%
  • Software-deployment tool wrapping Metakit.exe and calling setup.exe via PSAppDeployToolkit
  • Sandbox / dev machine running FireAnt sample for analysis
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessSignatureStatus != "Signed" or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "FireAnt"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the dropped setup.exe SHA256 and compare against the article's SHA1s; check the metakit.fireant.vn update URL the parent process resolved (DeviceNetworkEvents within ±10 min on same DeviceId). 2) Contain: network-isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill Metakit.exe + setup.exe, preserve the binary for triage. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId across DeviceImageLoadEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll loads in the next 24h and DeviceNetworkEvents to financemachinelearning.com / gatewayrvcenter.com — confirms the SPECTRALVIPER injection completed.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
| where FileName =~ "setup.exe"
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has "Metakit.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has "setup.exe"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName,
          ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, SHA1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit.exe Spawning setup.exe From User-Writable Path
id: 1e63a4f2-7d8b-4c5a-a1c7-9d3e2f4b8c01
description: Detects FireAnt Metakit.exe (Vietnamese stock-investor client) spawning a child setup.exe — the SPECTRALVIPER staging chain used in the OceanLotus FireAnt Metakit supply-chain attack reported by ESET.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
author: ThreatHuntingNarwhal
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Metakit.exe'
  selection_child:
    - Image|endswith: '\setup.exe'
    - Image|contains:
        - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
        - '\Users\Public\'
        - '\ProgramData\'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Metakit auto-update if FireAnt eventually ships signed installers (verify update server cert)
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:4688) (@ParentImage:(*\\Metakit.exe OR *\\metakit.exe OR *\\METAKIT.EXE) OR @ParentProcessName:(*\\Metakit.exe OR *\\metakit.exe)) (@Image:(*\\setup.exe OR *\\Setup.exe OR *\\SETUP.EXE) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\setup.exe OR *\\Setup.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^Metakit\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\setup\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public|ProgramData)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" AND (Processes.process_name="setup.exe" OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" AND (Processes.process_name="setup.exe" OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load — DtlCrashCatch.dll dropped/loaded from non-system path AIInstallation High
Catches the SPECTRALVIPER staging DLL 'DtlCrashCatch.dll' being written to disk or image-loaded from anywhere outside System32/WinSxS. ESET names this exact DLL as the side-loaded rogue payload after the FireAnt update chain — and the same DLL name appears in the Vietnamese transport-construction intrusion, so it's a stable IOC across both 2024–2026 OceanLotus clusters. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is the article's named rogue side-load DLL — extremely high-fidelity string with near-zero benign collisions outside System32/WinSxS. ESET names the same DLL across both the FireAnt cluster and the transport-construction intrusion, confirming it as a stable cross-campaign IOC; Elastic's 2023 write-up describes the same side-loading pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-research VM with the sample copied to %Temp% for analysis (whitelist analyst hostnames)
  • Red-team tooling re-using the DtlCrashCatch.dll name as a tongue-in-cheek IOC test
  • Backup / DFIR collector zipping the DLL into an evidence folder (FileCreated under \Evidence\)
  • Legitimate Acrobat / OneDrive component that happens to ship a same-named DLL in a future build (verify InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("securityresearcher","dfir-collector") and not (FolderPath has @"\Evidence\" or FolderPath has @"\Malware-Analysis\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: SHA1/SHA256 the dropped DLL and compare against the article's SHA1 list (865A1739..., B0FEA981..., 48FEBB91..., 511B7745..., 8CD78B8D...). Check parent process — was it the FireAnt Metakit chain or a different entry point? 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, kill any process with DtlCrashCatch.dll currently loaded (cross-reference DeviceImageLoadEvents → DeviceProcessEvents on InitiatingProcessId), quarantine the DLL file. 3) Hunt: pivot the parent SHA256 (the legit signed binary being abused) across the fleet for other side-load victims; check DeviceNetworkEvents for any subsequent C2 calls to the article's domains.
union
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
   | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
   | where FolderPath !has @"\Windows\System32\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
   | project Timestamp, Source="FileWrite", DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
   | where FolderPath !has @"\Windows\System32\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
   | project Timestamp, Source="ImageLoad", DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| where TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\System32\" and TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\" and TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SPECTRALVIPER Side-Load DLL DtlCrashCatch.dll Created In Non-System Path
id: 9b2d8c4a-5e3f-4d6c-b8a1-2c47e9f3a812
description: Detects creation or image-load of DtlCrashCatch.dll outside Windows system directories — the OceanLotus / SPECTRALVIPER side-loading stager named by ESET in the FireAnt Metakit and Vietnamese transport-construction campaigns.
references:

author: ThreatHuntingNarwhal

detection:

  filter_legit:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Windows\System32\'
      - '\Windows\SysWOW64\'
      - '\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(11 OR 7) @TargetFilename:(*\\DtlCrashCatch.dll OR *\\dtlcrashcatch.dll OR *\\DTLCRASHCATCH.DLL)) AND NOT (@TargetFilename:(*\\Windows\\System32\\* OR *\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\* OR *\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\DtlCrashCatch\.dll$/i
| NOT regex("\\\\Windows\\\\(System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)\\\\", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="DtlCrashCatch.dll" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*","*\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="DtlCrashCatch.dll" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*","*\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe AIInstallation High
Detects OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe — abused by SPECTRALVIPER as the injection host — talking to the named C2 infrastructure or any non-Microsoft public destination. Per ESET, DtlCrashCatch.dll injects itself into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe to launch the backdoor, so subsequent egress from that PID is the injection success signal. Rationale: OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe is the article's named injection target and the C2 domains/IPs come straight from the IOC bundle. Any OneDrive-named process talking to financemachinelearning.com / gatewayrvcenter.com is a definitive SPECTRALVIPER signal — Microsoft's real OneDrive client never resolves either. Note: Sentinel ASIM ImNetworkSession lacks process attribution, so the Sentinel detection falls back to raw Sysmon EID 3 via the Event table where EventData carries both Image and DestinationHostname. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1055.001 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-research lab detonating SPECTRALVIPER sample (whitelist the malware-analysis subnet)
  • Sysmon EventData truncation where Image and DestinationHostname appear in different events — verify with the matching EID 1 process create
  • ProcessName collision if a future malware family also uses the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe injection host (still high-fidelity given the C2 IPs)
  • Custom OneDrive sync client built in-house and routed through a hosting provider whose IP overlaps an IOC (extremely unlikely)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessSHA256 for the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe instance — if it differs from a known Microsoft hash, the binary itself was swapped (rare); if Microsoft-signed, the process was injected. Confirm with a DeviceImageLoadEvents query for DtlCrashCatch.dll on the same DeviceId in the prior 1h. 2) Contain: isolate the host, suspend the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe process (don't kill — memory forensics), block the C2 IPs at perimeter, kill the Metakit.exe parent if still running. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host that resolved/connected to the C2 list in the past 90 days, sweep for DtlCrashCatch.dll, and check public-facing MSSQL servers (the article notes that's the other initial-access vector OceanLotus used).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com")
   or RemoteIP in ("38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Source =~ "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 3
| where EventData has "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where EventData has_any ("financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com","38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, RenderedDescription, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OceanLotus / SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure callouts AICommand & Control Medium
Broad sweep for any host touching the OceanLotus C2 domains or IPs from ESET's IOC bundle — regardless of which process did it. Catches the injection chain on hosts where the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe technique was substituted with one of the three SPECTRALVIPER variants ESET observed on the transport-construction network. Rationale: All six domains and eight IPs come straight from ESET's IOC bundle on the SPECTRALVIPER / FireAnt clusters — no overlap with legitimate Vietnamese financial infrastructure. The hostnames don't pivot off any known parked/CDN ranges so a hit is effectively definitive. Cross-checked against MITRE G0050 (APT32 / OceanLotus) prior C2 patterns at https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper

Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel feed connector resolving the IOCs for ingestion (filter on InitiatingProcessFileName in known TI agents)
  • Security researcher visiting the domain in a sandbox VM
  • TI vendor's URLScan / VirusTotal scanner traffic if egress is mixed with prod
  • SOC analyst manually nslookup-ing the IOC from a jumphost
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("misp-modules","taxii2-client.exe","virustotal-cli.exe") and Computer !startswith "SOC-JUMP-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess on the matching host — if it's OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe / Metakit.exe / a signed binary with an oddly-located DLL, treat as confirmed. Pull the host's last 24h of process tree. 2) Contain: block the entire IOC list at the egress proxy, isolate the host, force password reset for the user, and (if MSSQL-facing) check sa-account logons going back to Nov 2024 (the article's earliest known transport-construction intrusion date). 3) Hunt: re-scope the DNS query to your full historical retention (90d+) — even one prior hit means the actor likely retained access well before today. Sweep for DtlCrashCatch.dll and the article's SHA1s across all endpoints.

   | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=coalesce(DstHostname, Url), QueryType=NetworkApplicationProtocol, Source="Network"),

SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 IOC sightings — file write, process exec, image load AIInstallation High
Pure-IOC sweep for the five SHA1 hashes ESET published for SPECTRALVIPER samples and stagers. Catches a hit even if the actor reuses the binary in a future cluster that swaps the C2 domains or parent binary. Rationale: The five SHA1s come straight from ESET's IOC bundle on this campaign — pure-hash hits have effectively zero false-positive rate. Sweeping across DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceFileEvents, and DeviceImageLoadEvents catches the binary regardless of where in the chain it appears (dropper, side-loaded DLL, or injected payload). Cross-referenced with MITRE G0050 and Elastic Security Labs' SPECTRALVIPER analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1027 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel feed agent caching the sample for sandbox detonation (whitelist the TI tooling host)
  • DFIR responder copying the binary onto a collection share for offline analysis
  • AV/EDR vendor signature lookup downloading the hash as a test
  • Sample uploaded to internal malware-zoo storage and indexed by file-scan agents
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("misp-svc","vt-collector") and DeviceName !startswith "MALWARE-ZOO-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the hit isn't your own SOC tooling (TI feed, malware zoo). Pull the parent process and file lineage on the host — was it dropped by Metakit.exe, downloaded over the web, or sideloaded from an Acrobat / OneDrive component? 2) Contain: quarantine the file via Defender Live Response, network-isolate the host, kill any process matching the SHA1, capture process memory before termination if forensics is needed. 3) Hunt: search the entire SHA256 set against the EDR fleet for 90d history; pivot the parent SHA256 (the legit side-loaded binary) for other side-load attempts; check the article's C2 IOCs from this host going back 18 months — the transport-construction intrusion ran Nov 2024 → Feb 2026, so dwell time can be substantial.
let SViperHashes = dynamic([
  "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D",
  "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194",
  "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947",
  "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB",
  "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (SViperHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (SViperHashes)
   | project Timestamp, Source="Process", DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
             ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (SViperHashes)
   | project Timestamp, Source="FileWrite", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName,
             FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (SViperHashes)
   | project Timestamp, Source="ImageLoad", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName,
             FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let SViperHashes = dynamic([
  "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D",
  "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194",
  "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947",
  "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB",
  "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
   | where SHA1 in (SViperHashes) or Hash in (SViperHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, Source="Process", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
             ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA1),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
   | where TargetFileSHA1 in (SViperHashes) or Hash in (SViperHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, Source="FileEvent", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
             ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName="", SHA1=TargetFileSHA1)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 connection to ESET-disclosed IPs/domains · [LLM] First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 connection to ESET-disclosed IPs/domains AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any outbound network connection to the eight SPECTRALVIPER C2 IPs and six C&C domains ESET published for OceanLotus's 2024-2026 FireAnt Metakit supply-chain and Vietnamese construction-corp campaigns. High-fidelity because every IOC is a known-bad C2 endpoint with no documented benign use. Rationale: Every IP and domain in this query is a SPECTRALVIPER C&C endpoint published in ESET's Table 2 and IOC bundle for the 2024-2026 OceanLotus campaigns; financemachinelearning.com is explicitly named as the C&C domain for the stable SPECTRALVIPER variant. Match by IP catches direct fallback; match by URL catches HTTPS proxied through hostname.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox / malware-analysis VM intentionally detonating SPECTRALVIPER samples
  • Threat-intel scrapers / Shodan-style researchers actively probing the IOC set
  • Security-tool URL-categorization scans of the malicious domains (e.g. Zscaler, Netskope)
  • Legitimate hosts that happen to be on a shared-IP CDN that now resolves to one of these IPs (rare — most IOCs are bare hosting)
  • DNS sinkhole responses if these domains have been sinkholed by a TI provider
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","iexplore.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the full process tree from DeviceProcessEvents for InitiatingProcessFileName at the time of the connection — confirm whether the originator is a known good binary (security tooling, sandbox) or an unsigned binary in a temp/AppData path matching SPECTRALVIPER drop patterns. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the device via Defender Live Response or EDR network-isolation, block the matched IP/domain at firewall and EDR network indicator policy, force credential reset for the InitiatingProcessAccountName. 3) HUNT: pivot on DeviceFileEvents for SHA1 against the 20-hash IOC set; query DnsEvents for the other five C&C domains across all hosts in the last 90 days; search for any FireAnt Metakit installs (file path or process name) on neighboring hosts and check their update history for a malicious payload window of Oct-2025 to Mar-2026.

SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write AIInstallation High
Alerts whenever a process executes or a file is written whose SHA1 matches one of the 20 SPECTRALVIPER / OceanLotus stager and dropper hashes ESET published. Covers both SPECTRALVIPER backdoor binaries and the malicious FireAnt Metakit update payloads from the supply-chain wave. Rationale: All 20 SHA1s are pulled directly from the IOC block of the ESET report and correspond to SPECTRALVIPER samples (both old reused first-iteration samples and fresh stable-version samples from Table 1) plus the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain droppers. Hash match on process + filesystem + image-load catches dropper, persistent loader, and DLL side-load variants.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike sample-submission VMs ingesting the IOC bundle for testing
  • DFIR teams replaying confirmed malware samples during tabletop exercises
  • VirusTotal / hybrid-analysis collector hosts that store hash archives
  • Security researcher endpoints reverse-engineering the samples
  • Backup/restore restoring a previously-quarantined sample from shadow copy
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "malware" and DeviceName !has "detonation"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify whether the host is a known malware-analysis sandbox or a production endpoint — check device tags, OU membership and the user profile of InitiatingProcessAccountName. If production, this is a confirmed-malicious detection with no investigation needed before action. 2) CONTAIN: network-isolate the device, kill the process tree, quarantine the binary, force credential rotation for any account with an interactive logon to that host in the last 90 days, and block the SHA1 across the EDR fleet via Indicators of Compromise policy. 3) HUNT: for every host that ran one of these hashes, pull DeviceNetworkEvents and DnsEvents 30 days back looking for the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains and eight IPs; check FireAnt Metakit install history; pivot on the InitiatingProcessFolderPath to identify the dropper that wrote the sample.

FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the FireAnt Metakit application (the Vietnamese stock-investment platform whose update server OceanLotus compromised from Oct-2025 to Mar-2026) spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or unsigned binaries from temp/AppData. This is the textbook detection shape for the supply-chain payload that ESET observed delivering SPECTRALVIPER after a poisoned update. Rationale: ESET explicitly names FireAnt Metakit as the compromised stock-trading platform and describes the update-server-replaced-with-malicious-payload pattern; any FireAnt Metakit process spawning a script interpreter, LOLBin, or binary out of temp/AppData is the operational shape of the supply-chain payload chain that ends in SPECTRALVIPER drop. Hunting tier because FireAnt's own update process may legitimately invoke some installer LOLBins on first install.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt Metakit update invoking msiexec.exe during a real product update
  • FireAnt installer writing helper binaries to %TEMP% as part of normal first-run installation
  • Endpoint backup software (Veeam, Acronis) interacting with FireAnt install directory during scheduled backup
  • User troubleshooting FireAnt by running it from a portable/extracted location in Downloads
  • Antivirus / DLP scanning FireAnt binaries on a schedule and reading from AppData
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessSignatureStatus != "Valid" or ChildSHA256 !in~ (toscalar(DeviceFileCertificateInfo | where IsSigned == true and SignatureType == "CodeSign" | summarize make_set(SHA256)))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the FireAnt Metakit installer SHA256 and version from InitiatingProcessSHA256 / VersionInfoProductVersion and compare against the vendor's published known-good hash; check the timestamp against ESET's Oct-2025 to Mar-2026 supply-chain window — any install in that range is suspect by default. 2) CONTAIN: if the parent SHA256 is unknown or in the known-bad set, isolate the host, kill the process tree, and quarantine all files written by the child process in the prior 24h; alert the user to discontinue use of FireAnt Metakit pending vendor confirmation. 3) HUNT: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the host for any of the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains in the 7 days after the install; pivot DeviceFileEvents for files written by InitiatingProcessFolderPath of FireAnt to identify dropped stagers; check for any other endpoints in the org running FireAnt and audit their install times.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "fireant"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where ParentProcessName has "fireant" or ActingProcessName has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Supply-Chain Update Spawning Suspicious Child
id: 9f1c5e22-3a7d-4f44-8e91-2f4a8b9c0d11
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or binaries from temp/AppData. ESET attributes a compromised-update-server supply-chain attack (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026) on this product to OceanLotus / APT32 that resulted in SPECTRALVIPER deployment.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  suspicious_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'

    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  condition: parent and (suspicious_child or suspicious_path)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit*)) (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\msiexec.exe) OR @Image:(*\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\AppData\Roaming\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Windows\Temp\* OR *\Users\Public\*))

| ParentBaseFileName=/fireant|metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/(FireAnt|Metakit)/i
| (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|msiexec)\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|AppData\\\\Roaming|ProgramData|Windows\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ImageFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any internal host making a first-time HTTPS connection to a domain matching the SPECTRALVIPER C&C naming pattern ESET catalogued (single-word .com domains posing as services - finance/cyber/sync/design themed), where the domain is unseen across the org's 30-day baseline. Designed to catch the next OceanLotus C2 rotation before the IOC list updates. Rationale: Uses the explicit six SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains from ESET Table 2 AND a baseline anti-join so any first-time-in-org connection to a similarly-shaped domain (finance/cyber/services themed single-word .coms — the OceanLotus naming convention) gets flagged. Catches IOC rotation that won't be in the next ESET update.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing/finance department visiting a newly-launched legitimate fintech site for the first time
  • User clicking a phishing-link analysis service that proxies through similar-shape domains
  • Threat-intel browser extension fetching from a sandbox URL
  • Internal CI/CD reaching a newly-provisioned vendor SaaS subdomain
  • Domain typosquats of legitimate companies (separate detection class)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","opera.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: enrich the matched domain with WHOIS / registration date and passive DNS - any domain registered in the last 90 days with low passive-DNS history and matching the SPECTRALVIPER naming theme is high-suspicion; check InitiatingProcessFileName to see whether it's a browser (often FP) or an unsigned binary (almost always TP). 2) CONTAIN: if non-browser process or unsigned binary, isolate the host, sinkhole the domain via DNS RPZ, and block at proxy/firewall; if browser, push the URL to your secure-browsing/SWG block-list pending vendor categorization. 3) HUNT: across the fleet, search the last 90 days for any prior connection to the same domain or any of the six known SPECTRALVIPER C&Cs; pivot on the matched host for any of the 20 SHA1 SPECTRALVIPER hashes and for FireAnt Metakit install activity.
let BaselineDomains = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceId) by Domain
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_pattern = @"(?i)(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$";
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
| where Domain matches regex ioc_pattern or Domain matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on Domain
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, Domain, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let BaselineDomains = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(SrcIpAddr) by DnsQuery=tolower(DnsQuery)
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_known = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend DnsQueryLower = tolower(DnsQuery)
| where DnsQueryLower has_any (ioc_known) or DnsQueryLower matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on $left.DnsQueryLower == $right.DnsQuery
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:22 (@QueryName:(*financemachinelearning.com OR *gatewayrvcenter.com OR *coachcybersecurity.com OR *mxprodesign.com OR *power-sync-services.com OR *leadingfilipinoteams.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, FirstIP4Record], function=count(), function=min(@timestamp))
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 11 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

npm install lifecycle hook spawning shell or LOLBin (preinstall/install/postinstall) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the core attack surface the article calls out — preinstall/install/postinstall scripts running during `npm install`. Flags node/npm spawning shells, script hosts or download LOLBins, which is how a compromised transitive dependency would gain code execution on a developer or CI runner. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named lifecycle hooks (`preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`) and the `npm install` command — described as 'the single largest code-execution surface in the npm ecosystem'. Parent=node/npm with child=interpreter/LOLBin is the exact behaviour npm v12 is blocking by default. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/npm/cli/releases • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/using-npm/scripts
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp builds legitimately spawning cmd.exe for native compile (electron, sharp, node-sass)
  • Husky pre-commit hooks invoking sh.exe under WSL during local development
  • Internal devops tooling distributed as npm packages that wrap PowerShell scripts
  • Yarn/pnpm migrations that call npm-cli.js with a legitimate postinstall hook on first run
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildImage endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ParentCmd has_any ("node-gyp","binding.gyp","prebuild-install"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect ChildCmd and ParentCmd — is the child a build tool (node-gyp/cmake/cl.exe — likely benign) or a generic shell/LOLBin reaching the network (suspicious)? Pull the package name from cwd and check it against the org allowlist + npm advisories. 2) Contain: isolate the host or CI runner; revoke any npm auth tokens stored on it (~/.npmrc); pause CI jobs that ran the same install. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceName for outbound connections from node.exe in the next 60 min (see related UC), file writes to %APPDATA%/%TEMP%, and AAD/Okta tokens issued from that workstation post-install.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js","npm install","npm i ")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe","sh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","postinstall","npm run install","lifecycle")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe")
   or CommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js","npm install","npm i ")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe","sh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
   or CommandLine has_any ("preinstall","postinstall","npm run install","lifecycle")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
