Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable SAP NetWeaver / Ivanti Sentry / FortiSandbox version inventory (June 2026 patch wave) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Ivanti Sentry MICS handleMessage endpoint exploitation attempt (CVE-2026-10520 / CVE-2026-10523) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Ivanti Sentry MICS handleMessage endpoint exploitation attempt (CVE-2026-10520 / CVE-2026-10523) AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP requests targeting the Ivanti Sentry MICS configuration endpoint `/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage`, identified by watchTowr Labs as the vulnerable path used by CVE-2026-10520 (unauthenticated RCE via the handleExecute() backend) and the companion auth-bypass CVE-2026-10523. Pre-patch Sentry instances (before R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1) reach this path without authentication; post-patch they redirect to the login page. Rationale: Pivots on the literal URL path watchTowr Labs disclosed as the vulnerable endpoint — `/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage`. This string does not appear in any legitimate MobileIron/Ivanti Sentry traffic outside of exploitation attempts. Defender Advanced Hunting is left empty because the Sentry appliance is not a Windows endpoint and its inbound HTTP traffic is not in DeviceNetworkEvents (RemoteUrl is outbound-only). Cross-checked against the watchTowr Labs disclosure cited in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.watchtowr.com/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ivanti-fortinet-and-sap-release-patches.html
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanner (Tenable Nessus / Qualys / Rapid7) probing the endpoint as part of CVE-2026-10520 detection plugins
  • Pentest engagement replicating the watchTowr PoC against the Sentry appliance
  • Ivanti support engineer running a remote diagnostic that touches the MICS configuration API
  • Security researcher running a Nuclei template against the org's external attack surface
  • Internal patch-verification probe by IT confirming the post-patch redirect to login behaviour
Suppression filter
// Add to Sentinel query — suppress known scanner IPs and authorised testing windows
| where SourceIP !in ("<tenable_scanner_ip>", "<qualys_scanner_ip>")
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus", "qualys", "Nuclei", "watchTowr")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Resolve the source IP — geolocation, ASN, prior 30-day history against the Sentry appliance. Cross-reference against the authorised vuln-scanner allowlist and any active red-team window. Pull the full HTTP request body if WAF captured it; legitimate MICS calls do not transit this path from external clients. Step 2 (Contain): If the source is external and unsanctioned, block the IP at the perimeter WAF and confirm the Sentry appliance is at R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1 (the patch redirects unauthenticated requests to the login page). Snapshot the appliance for forensics. Step 3 (Hunt): On the Sentry host look for net-new admin accounts created in the management UI (CVE-2026-10523 outcome), unexpected root-level command execution in the Tomcat/MICS process tree, and outbound connections from the appliance to unknown hosts. Pivot on the source IP against your external-facing assets for parallel exploitation attempts.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
| extend AttackerIP = SourceIP, SentryHost = coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationIP)
| project TimeGenerated, AttackerIP, SentryHost, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction, ReceivedBytes, SentBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable SAP NetWeaver / Ivanti Sentry / FortiSandbox version inventory (June 2026 patch wave) AIReconnaissance High
Hunts for managed endpoints and servers running versions of SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP/Java, Ivanti Sentry, FortiSandbox, or SAP Commerce Cloud affected by the seven critical CVEs released on 2026-06-10. Surfaces pre-patch instances of CVE-2026-25089, CVE-2026-10520, CVE-2026-10523, CVE-2026-44748, CVE-2026-27671, CVE-2026-22732, and CVE-2026-40128 so they can be prioritised before public PoCs surface. Rationale: Uses the seven CVE IDs verbatim from the article body as the filter set, joined to DeviceInfo to prioritise internet-facing assets — the exposure surface that matters most given watchTowr's confirmation of unauthenticated RCE on Ivanti Sentry. Falcon LogScale, Datadog, and CloudWatch are intentionally empty because TVM-style inventory is a Defender XDR capability and these CVEs primarily affect appliances/servers that don't ship endpoint telemetry to those platforms. For FortiSandbox and Ivanti Sentry appliances not enrolled in MDE, the runbook directs analysts to the CMDB. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ivanti-fortinet-and-sap-release-patches.html
ATT&CKT1592.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SAP NetWeaver instance is patched at the kernel/SP level but TVM has not yet refreshed (lag up to 24h after patch deployment)
  • Air-gapped lab/test SAP system flagged but not reachable from production network
  • FortiSandbox appliance not visible to MDE — TVM misses it entirely (asset-inventory gap, not a true positive)
  • Ivanti Sentry version string parsed incorrectly by the TVM scanner when running a hot-fix build
  • Device flagged as IsInternetFacing=true but actually behind an internal-only load balancer due to misclassified public IP
Suppression filter
// Optional — exclude lab/test machine groups and unmanaged-asset placeholders
| where MachineGroup !in ("Lab-SAP-Sandbox", "DevTest-NetWeaver", "Decommissioned")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Sort results by IsInternetFacing desc then by CVSS — CVE-2026-10520 (CVSS 10.0, unauth root RCE on Sentry) and CVE-2026-27671 (CVSS 9.8, unauth memory corruption on SAP RFC) are the immediate priorities. Confirm each finding against the CMDB owner. Step 2 (Contain): For internet-facing pre-patch systems: restrict ingress to known management IPs at the firewall, then schedule emergency patch windows to FortiSandbox 5.0.6 / 4.4.9, Ivanti Sentry R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1, and the latest SAP Security Notes for the four SAP CVEs. Step 3 (Hunt): For each affected system pull the prior 14 days of inbound web/RFC traffic. On Ivanti Sentry pivot to the companion UC for `/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage` access. On SAP, audit SAML AuthnResponse messages for duplicate Signature/Assertion blocks (CVE-2026-44748 wrapping) and look for malformed RFC packets to the dispatcher (CVE-2026-27671).

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Assets exposed to CISA KEV CVEs added 2026-06-10 (Cisco SD-WAN, Chrome V8, Arista EOS) AIExploitation High
Surfaces every endpoint in TVM that still carries CVE-2026-20245, CVE-2026-11645, or CVE-2026-7473 — the three flaws CISA added to the KEV catalog on 2026-06-10. Used to drive prioritised remediation against the FCEB-mandated 2026-06-23 patch deadline and to identify internet-facing assets first. Rationale: Pivots directly on the three CVE IDs named in the article and the FCEB 2026-06-23 deadline; joins DeviceInfo to prioritise IsInternetFacing assets where the Chrome V8 and Cisco SD-WAN Manager flaws have the largest blast radius.
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Asset has been patched within the last 24h but the TVM scan has not yet refreshed its software inventory
  • End-of-life Chrome installations on kiosk/lab machines that are intentionally air-gapped
  • Arista 7020R/7280R/7500R appliances reported via third-party ingestion where SoftwareVersion is unparsed and TVM reports the whole device family as vulnerable
  • Embedded Chrome (CEF / Electron shells) on the host being flagged under the Chrome V8 CVE when the embedded runtime is not actually exposed to attacker-controlled HTML
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "unknown" and isnotempty(SoftwareVersion)
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate the affected hosts, split by IsInternetFacing and by CVE; for Arista hits also confirm whether the device is actually configured as a VXLAN VTEP, GRE endpoint, or has an IP decap-group (the precondition Arista calls out — non-tunnel-endpoints are not exploitable). 2) Contain: for Chrome V8, push the emergency stable-channel update via Intune/SCCM; for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, apply the vendor advisory; for Arista (no patch planned) deploy the upstream or on-device ACLs Arista documented to selectively allow only legitimate tunnel traffic. 3) Hunt: pivot the confirmed-vulnerable host list into DeviceProcessEvents / DeviceNetworkEvents for the prior 14 days looking for already-landed payloads — especially Chrome renderer→shell pivots covered by the companion detection in this set.

Chrome renderer process spawning shell or LOLBin (CVE-2026-11645 V8 sandbox-escape behaviour) AIExploitation Medium
Detects a Chrome renderer child process (chrome.exe launched with --type=renderer) spawning a shell, scripting host, or LOLBin. This is the textbook post-RCE breakout shape for CVE-2026-11645, the V8 out-of-bounds R/W that gives the attacker code execution inside the renderer sandbox and requires a follow-on sandbox escape to reach the user shell. Rationale: --type=renderer is the canonical Chromium flag that identifies a sandboxed renderer; pairing it with a shell/LOLBin child is the minimum-noise expression of the V8 sandbox-escape shape called out in the article (CVE-2026-11645 — 'execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page'). No Chrome process in normal use shells out from the renderer tier.
ATT&CKT1203 T1189 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Selenium / Playwright / Puppeteer browser-automation harnesses where a page script intentionally shells out via a native-messaging host
  • Enterprise browser-isolation or DLP agents (e.g. Menlo, Forcepoint) that legitimately spawn helper processes from the renderer container
  • Chrome OS-update mechanism on developer/Canary builds invoking helper utilities (rare on stable channel)
  • Custom CEF/Electron-wrapped enterprise apps where chrome.exe is actually the embedded runtime spawning the app's own helpers
  • Chromium-based PDF/print-preview features briefly spawning a renderer helper that touches PrintIsolated.exe — not in the LOLBin list but worth noting on triage
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--enable-automation","--remote-debugging-port","--headless") and AccountName has_any ("selenium","puppeteer","playwright","buildagent"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the parent renderer's full command line and walk back DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId/Pid in the prior 60s to identify the URL/host that served the exploit page; capture child cmdline and SHA256. 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, kill the Chrome process tree, and preserve %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cache for IR. Block the source domain at the proxy/DNS RPZ. 3) Hunt: pivot on the child SHA256 and any dropped payload paths in the user profile / Temp across the fleet; query DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory to enumerate every host still below the Chrome version that fixes CVE-2026-11645 and drive emergency rollout.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--type=renderer"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "chrome.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "--type=renderer"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Chrome Renderer Spawning Shell or LOLBin (CVE-2026-11645 V8 Sandbox Escape)
id: a8b4f230-7c92-4d83-9e3a-21f5c8b4e190
description: Detects a Chrome renderer process (chrome.exe --type=renderer) spawning a shell, scripting host, or LOLBin — the expected post-exploitation shape of CVE-2026-11645 V8 sandbox-escape activity.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
    ParentCommandLine|contains: '--type=renderer'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Browser automation / Selenium harnesses shelling out from page scripts
  - Enterprise DLP or browser-isolation agents that legitimately spawn helpers from the renderer
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\CHROME.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:*--type\=renderer* @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/chrome\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
| _count > 0
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as child_hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" AND Processes.parent_process="*--type=renderer*" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") AND Processes.user!="*$" by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as child_hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" AND Processes.parent_process="*--type=renderer*" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") AND Processes.user!="*$" by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Access pattern to go-base admin/refresh endpoints with Bearer auth
Web probing for exposed dev.env / .env config files (CVE-2026-48031 disclosure) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for HTTP requests targeting common config-file paths (.env, dev.env, .env.bak) on web servers. Attackers scan for the dev.env file containing AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random to harvest the hardcoded JWT signing key from go-base deployments. Rationale: Direct hit on the article's `dev.env:10 AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random` template-default disclosure path. Pre-forgery recon — attackers grep public GitHub for go-base then probe live deployments for the same template paths. Web-server / WAF / ImWebSession is the natural telemetry; cloudwatch_query is empty because this is HTTP-layer telemetry against the app, not a CloudTrail signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1592 T1552.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Detectify) sweeping known sensitive paths during authorised scans
  • Bug-bounty researchers on scope hitting common config paths
  • Pentesters using OWASP ZAP / Burp Active Scan against staging
  • CI/CD smoke-tests that include .env probes in their default checklist
  • Static-content health-check probes from misconfigured upstream load balancers
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in (dynamic(["<corp-scanner-1>","<corp-scanner-2>"]))
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Detectify","Burp","ZAP")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the source IP, user-agent, and full HTTP path; check whether the scStatus was 200 (potential disclosure) vs 404 (just a probe). Pivot on the source IP — is it part of a corporate-scanner allow-list (Qualys, Tenable) or an external scanner ASN? Step 2 (contain): if any 200, immediately rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a strong 32+ byte value (`openssl rand -base64 32`), invalidate all outstanding refresh tokens, and add WAF rules blocking dot-env paths. Step 3 (hunt): search the same source IP for subsequent /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh hits (sibling UC), and grep GitHub / pastebins for leaks of your AUTH_JWT_SECRET value.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("dev.env", ".env", "dev.env.bak", ".env.bak", ".env.orig", "dev.env.orig")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("go.exe","dlv.exe","code.exe","goland64.exe","git.exe","explorer.exe","devenv.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let ConfigPaths = dynamic(["/dev.env","/.env","/.env.bak","/dev.env.bak","/.env.orig","/dev.env.orig","/.env~"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has_any (ConfigPaths)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Access pattern to go-base admin/refresh endpoints with Bearer auth AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for HTTP requests to the go-base API endpoints described in the article PoC — /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh — accompanied by Bearer tokens. After forging a JWT with the hardcoded `random` secret, attackers fan out across these specific paths to harvest user data and rotate to fresh forged tokens. Rationale: Article PoC explicitly hits these three endpoints (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh) sequentially with a Bearer token forged from secret=`random`. Source IP touching 2+ of them in a short window with a Bearer header is the article-specific shape — generic Bearer auth alone would be too noisy. defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query / cloudwatch_query are empty: this is server-side web-tier telemetry that Defender XDR Advanced Hunting, Falcon EDR, and AWS CloudTrail do not naturally surface — they don't see inbound HTTP path + Authorization headers on the API server. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
ATT&CKT1078 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin user during routine user-management work (stable IP + corporate UA + MFA-backed session)
  • Internal load-testing or smoke-tests of the go-base API hitting the same paths
  • Front-end SPA polling /api/v1/me after every navigation and refreshing tokens on a schedule
  • Postman/Insomnia developer manual testing during local QA
  • API documentation generators (Swagger UI, Redoc) exercising the endpoint list
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in (dynamic(["<corp-admin-jumpbox-1>","<corp-admin-jumpbox-2>"]))
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Postman","PostmanRuntime","Insomnia","smoke-test","Swagger","Redoc")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): for the source IP, capture the full Authorization header (where the WAF logs it), base64-decode the JWT payload, and confirm whether the token validates against secret=`random` (try jwt.io or `python -c 'import jwt; jwt.decode(t, "random", algorithms=["HS256"])'`). If it validates, the token is forged. Step 2 (contain): rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32+ byte random value, apply PR#31's known-weak-secrets `log.Fatal` guard, bump the issuer key version to invalidate all outstanding tokens, then block the source IP at the WAF. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the JWT `sub` claim from the captured token — list every API call from that sub in the last 30 days; check GitHub / pastebin for leaks of your AUTH_JWT_SECRET value; correlate with the dev.env probing sibling UC on the same source IP.
let GoBasePaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin/users","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any (GoBasePaths)
| where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| where HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization startswith "Bearer "
| summarize Requests = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(Url), Paths = make_set(Url, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SuccessCount = countif(HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)) by SrcIpAddr, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| where DistinctPaths >= 2 or Requests >= 5
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:cloudflare OR source:aws.alb) (@http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/admin/users* OR */api/v1/me* OR */api/v1/token/refresh*) OR @http.url:(*/api/v1/admin/users* OR */api/v1/me* OR */api/v1/token/refresh*)) @http.request_headers.authorization:Bearer*
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses dc(Web.url) as distinct_paths from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/api/v1/admin/users*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/me*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/token/refresh*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where distinct_paths >= 2 OR count >= 5
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses dc(Web.url) as distinct_paths from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/api/v1/admin/users*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/me*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/token/refresh*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where distinct_paths >= 2 OR count >= 5
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Cargo/rustc build script spawning network or git utilities (build.rs LOLBin abuse) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound POST to onering Sentry exfil endpoint (o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io) · [LLM] curl/wget POST with Sentry envelope Content-Type spawned by build script · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cargo build-time git log/diff exfil pattern (onering build.rs) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Outbound POST to onering Sentry exfil endpoint (o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io) AICommand & Control High
Detects any host contacting the exact Sentry ingest endpoint hard-coded in the malicious onering 1.4.1 build.rs. The org ID o4511539639222272 and project ID 4511539669368912 are unique to the attacker's Sentry tenant and are the highest-fidelity IOC in the article. Rationale: The Sentry org ID (o4511539639222272), project ID (4511539669368912), and DSN public key (8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821) are unique attacker-controlled identifiers from the article body. Any traffic to this exact tenant is a direct compromise indicator. Cross-checked against the maintainer's GitHub issue (https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1) referenced in article. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://crates.io/crates/onering
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Sentry crash reporting from internal applications (would target your own org ID, not o4511539639222272)
  • Security researcher analyzing the IOC in a sandbox
  • Defender Network Protection or proxy that telemetry-mirrors blocked requests
  • Threat-intel platform fetching IOC for enrichment
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("<your-corp-sentry-org-id>", "<your-corp-sentry-project-id>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source host and the initiating process; pull cargo/build history and confirm whether onering 1.4.1 is in any Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock on the host. 2) Contain: isolate the developer workstation/build agent, rotate any source-code-signing certificates, GitHub tokens or SSH keys present on the host, and assume the most recent git commits' source diffs were leaked. 3) Hunt: pivot on `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo run` invocations across the fleet in the same window; search any other connection to *.ingest.de.sentry.io that does NOT match your organization's known Sentry DSNs; review GitHub repos for any crate.io dependencies on onering across all branches.

| where RemoteUrl has_any ("o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io", "4511539669368912/envelope", "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

Cargo build-time git log/diff exfil pattern (onering build.rs) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the exact two git invocations the malicious onering build.rs runs against the consumer's project: `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit":...}` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD`. These run unprompted as a child of cargo/rustc/build-script-build, which is a strong tell for crate-time code theft. Rationale: The article quotes the exact `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` invocation and the `--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H","author":"%an","email":"%ae","date":"%aI","subject":"%s"}` template. The combination (cargo→git, diff HEAD^ HEAD OR JSON pretty-format on `log -n 1`) is almost never produced by humans — IDEs/CI use different format strings. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1005 T1195.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer cargo plugin (e.g. cargo-release, cargo-edit) that legitimately introspects HEAD
  • CI step that emits build provenance from git log immediately after `cargo build`
  • Custom in-house cargo subcommand that wraps git for version stamping
  • Build.rs in a benign crate that embeds git commit hash into the binary
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cargo-release","cargo-edit","cargo-version","cargo-make") or ProcessCommandLine has "--pretty=format:%h" and not ProcessCommandLine has "author")
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the full command line; if `diff HEAD^ HEAD` is present, confirm whether the crate is onering 1.4.1 by checking the host's `Cargo.lock` and `~/.cargo/registry/src/*/onering-*`. 2) Contain: kill the cargo/rustc process tree, isolate the host, and treat the most recent git commit's diff as leaked — rotate any secrets that may have been touched. 3) Hunt: query the same parent-child shape across all dev/CI hosts; review network egress from those hosts to ingest.*.sentry.io and other crash-reporting domains; audit cargo dependency tree (`cargo tree`) on each impacted repo for onering and any siblings published by the same maintainer.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc","build-script-build.exe","build-script-build")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD", "diff HEAD~1 HEAD")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "log" and ProcessCommandLine has "-n 1" and ProcessCommandLine has "--pretty=format" and ProcessCommandLine has "%H" and ProcessCommandLine has "%an")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc","build-script-build.exe","build-script-build")
  | where CommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD","diff HEAD~1 HEAD")
     or (CommandLine has "log" and CommandLine has "-n 1" and CommandLine has "--pretty=format" and CommandLine has "%H")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("cargo","rustc","build-script-build")
  | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD","diff HEAD~1 HEAD")

  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

curl/wget POST with Sentry envelope Content-Type spawned by build script AICommand & Control High
Detects the exact HTTP request shape the onering build.rs builds with curl: POST to a Sentry envelope endpoint carrying `Content-Type: application/x-sentry-envelope`. The headers and envelope path together are a very narrow fingerprint and almost never appear in interactive shells or build pipelines unless Sentry CLI is in use. Rationale: The article literally prints the request: POST to `/api/4511539669368912/envelope/` with `Content-Type: application/x-sentry-envelope`. Legitimate Sentry telemetry is normally emitted by the Sentry SDK, not curl invoked from a build script — the parent-child constraint (cargo→curl→Sentry envelope) is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic LOLBin alert. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://docs.sentry.io/api/envelopes/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A team that uses the `sentry-cli` binary in a build step (would invoke `sentry-cli`, not raw curl, and would target your own org)
  • Custom CI script that legitimately uploads source maps to Sentry via curl
  • Developer manually testing a Sentry integration locally
  • Sentry self-hosted to internal envelope endpoint (filter by domain to exclude)
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("<your-org-sentry-id>","sentry-cli") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "sentry-cli")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full command line and extract the destination Sentry org/project IDs. If they match `o4511539639222272` / `4511539669368912`, treat as confirmed onering compromise. 2) Contain: kill the cargo/build process tree; revoke any credentials/tokens accessible from the build host (CI runner tokens, GitHub PATs, signing keys, AWS metadata); snapshot the host. 3) Hunt: search for the same envelope-POST shape org-wide for the last 90 days; pivot to any host that has ever resolved `o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io`; review developer repos for onering and other crates from the same maintainer (cenotelie).

| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("application/x-sentry-envelope","ingest.de.sentry.io/api/","/envelope/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc","build-script-build.exe","build-script-build")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc","build-script-build.exe","build-script-build")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","/curl","/wget")
  | where CommandLine has_any ("application/x-sentry-envelope","ingest.de.sentry.io/api/","/envelope/")

Cargo/rustc build script spawning network or git utilities (build.rs LOLBin abuse) AIInstallation Medium
Hunting query for Rust build scripts (`build-script-build` and direct children of `cargo`/`rustc`) spawning curl, wget, powershell, bash -c, sh -c, or git. Legitimate build scripts overwhelmingly stay inside the compiler and link toolchains; outbound network or repo introspection from a build script is the generic pattern that captures onering-class supply-chain code. Rationale: The article specifies the malicious behaviour runs from build.rs at compile time, with curl as the network egress and git as the data-collection tool. Filtering on the cargo/rustc/build-script-build parent process catches the pattern even if a future variant changes domain, headers, or hash — only the architectural shape stays constant. The leftanti-baseline join keeps the noise down on dev workstations where some cargo plugins legitimately shell out. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crates that legitimately invoke `pkg-config`/`bindgen` via shell (mostly stays in cc/clang, not curl)
  • Crates that embed git commit hash via `git rev-parse HEAD` in build.rs
  • Cargo subcommands like `cargo-audit` or `cargo-deny` shelling out to fetch advisory data
  • Build pipelines that wrap cargo with custom shell scripts (would show shell as parent, not cargo)
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git rev-parse HEAD","git describe","pkg-config","--cflags","--libs") and FileName !in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: list the crate behind the build-script-build by inspecting `target/debug/build/<crate>-<hash>/build-script-build` on the host; cross-reference with `Cargo.lock`. 2) Contain: if the crate or its child binary is unknown, isolate the host and quarantine the cargo registry cache (`~/.cargo/registry/src`, `~/.cargo/registry/cache`). 3) Hunt: run `cargo tree` against repos on the host to enumerate dependency parents; sweep the rest of the dev fleet for the same crate name; query DNS for any first-time external resolutions originating from build-script-build processes.
let BaselineDays = 30d;
let RecentHours = 24h;
let Baseline = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(BaselineDays) .. ago(RecentHours))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("build-script-build.exe","build-script-build","cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc")
    | summarize by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(RecentHours)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("build-script-build.exe","build-script-build","cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc")
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh","git.exe","git","nslookup.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let BaselineDays = 30d;
let RecentHours = 24h;
let Baseline = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(BaselineDays) .. ago(RecentHours))
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("build-script-build","cargo","rustc")
    | summarize by DvcHostname, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(RecentHours)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("build-script-build","cargo","rustc")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","powershell","pwsh","cmd.exe","bash","sh","git","nslookup","certutil","bitsadmin")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on DvcHostname, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) @ParentImage:(*\build-script-build* OR *\cargo.exe OR *\rustc.exe OR *\cargo OR *\rustc) @Image:(*\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\bash OR *\sh OR *\git.exe OR *\git OR *\nslookup.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(build-script-build|cargo|rustc)(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/(curl|wget|powershell|pwsh|cmd|bash|sh|git|nslookup|certutil|bitsadmin)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
| sort(count, order=desc)

phpBB admin control panel access without preceding successful authentication (CVE-2026-48611 post-exploit) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the article's core claim — a single unauthenticated HTTP request yields a valid session as any user, including administrators. Detects clients hitting phpBB's /adm/ control panel (or other authenticated-only endpoints) that have no prior successful login POST from the same source within the lookback. Web-access-log baseline anti-join; the auth bypass leaves no login event behind it. Rationale: Detects the article's headline claim: 'A single unauthenticated HTTP request is enough to obtain a valid session as any user' — manifests in web logs as access to /adm/ (the phpBB ACP path is a hardcoded, article-specific string) without any preceding POST to /ucp.php, /app.php/user/login, or the new /user/oauth/authenticate/ endpoint named in the article body. Cross-checked CVE-2026-48611 (the actual auth-bypass CVE per Bleeping Computer / Infosecurity-Magazine) and the phpBB 3.3.17 release announcement. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Session cookie-based access where the original login POST happened outside the lookback window (long-lived sessions)
  • Admin accessing ACP via SSO/OAuth where the login flow terminates on a different host that isn't in the same web-log stream
  • Internal monitoring/uptime probes (Pingdom, Datadog synthetics) hitting /adm/ via stored auth headers
  • Load balancer health checks misconfigured to probe /adm/ paths
  • Legitimate admins resuming a persistent session after a browser restart
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !contains "Pingdom" and csUserAgent !contains "Googlebot" and csUserAgent !contains "bingbot" and csUserAgent !contains "DatadogSynthetics" and csUserAgent !contains "UptimeRobot"
| where cIP !in ("<corp-monitoring-egress-1>", "<corp-monitoring-egress-2>")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the cIP's full request trail to the phpBB host in the last 24h — confirm there really is no login POST and no inherited session cookie carrying a known admin user. Geo-locate the cIP and check if it matches the admin's normal source. 2. Contain: if confirmed unauthenticated admin access, force-rotate the admin password, invalidate all phpBB sessions (truncate phpbb_sessions), confirm version is 3.3.17+ (upgrade now if not), and pull the running config to look for attacker-created admin accounts in phpbb_user_group (group_id 5/6). 3. Hunt: enumerate every phpBB instance in the estate (W3CIISLog/Apache access logs for /ucp.php or /viewforum.php), check each for the same anti-join pattern, and search the cIP against all internet-facing assets for parallel exploitation.
let Lookback = 7d;
let AdminHits = W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where csUriStem startswith "/adm/" or csUriStem =~ "/adm/index.php"
  | where scStatus in (200, 302)
  | project AdminTime = TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csUserName, csUserAgent, csMethod, sSiteName;
let LoginPosts = W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriStem in~ ("/ucp.php", "/app.php/user/login")
     or csUriStem startswith "/user/oauth/authenticate/"
     or (csUriStem =~ "/ucp.php" and csUriQuery has "mode=login")
  | where scStatus in (200, 302, 303)
  | project LoginTime = TimeGenerated, cIP, sSiteName;
AdminHits
| join kind=leftanti LoginPosts on cIP, sSiteName
| summarize FirstAdminHit = min(AdminTime), LastAdminHit = max(AdminTime),
            AdminRequests = count(), DistinctAdminPaths = dcount(csUriStem),
            SampleEndpoints = make_set(csUriStem, 10),
            UserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5)
            by cIP, sSiteName
| where AdminRequests >= 1
| order by FirstAdminHit desc
(source:nginx.access OR source:apache.access OR source:iis) (@http.url_details.path:(*/adm/index.php OR */adm/*)) @http.status_code:(200 OR 302) -@usr.id:* -@http.useragent:(*Googlebot* OR *bingbot* OR *Pingdom*)

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| join type=outer src dest [
    | tstats `summariesonly` count as login_post_count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/ucp.php*" OR Web.url="*/app.php/user/login*" OR Web.url="*/user/oauth/authenticate/*") Web.http_method=POST Web.status IN (200,302,303) by Web.src, Web.dest
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
  ]
| where isnull(login_post_count) OR login_post_count=0
| eval phpbb_admin_seen=strftime(first_admin_hit,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| stats sum(count) as admin_requests, dc(url) as distinct_admin_paths, values(methods) as methods, values(user_agents) as user_agents, min(first_admin_hit) as first_admin_hit by src, dest
| where admin_requests >= 1
| sort - first_admin_hit
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.http_method) as methods, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, min(_time) as first_admin_hit, max(_time) as last_admin_hit from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/adm/index.php*" OR Web.url="*/adm/*") Web.status IN (200,302) by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| join type=outer src dest [
    | tstats summariesonly=false count as login_post_count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/ucp.php*" OR Web.url="*/app.php/user/login*" OR Web.url="*/user/oauth/authenticate/*") Web.http_method=POST Web.status IN (200,302,303) by Web.src, Web.dest
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
  ]
| where isnull(login_post_count) OR login_post_count=0
| eval phpbb_admin_seen=strftime(first_admin_hit,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| stats sum(count) as admin_requests, dc(url) as distinct_admin_paths, values(methods) as methods, values(user_agents) as user_agents, min(first_admin_hit) as first_admin_hit by src, dest
| where admin_requests >= 1
| sort - first_admin_hit
Mass phpBB reconnaissance + authentication endpoint burst (CVE-2026-48611 mass exploitation) AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects the Santy-style scanning pattern the article explicitly recalls — a single source enumerating phpBB-specific endpoints (memberlist.php for target picking, then ucp.php / login / OAuth callbacks) in a tight time window. The article notes the default-public memberlist makes target selection trivial, so the scan-then-auth-bypass sequence is the most likely mass-exploitation shape. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit signature strings: memberlist.php (called out by name as the public default-on enumeration surface), ucp.php (phpBB user control panel), and the newly-named /user/oauth/authenticate/ post-patch path. The article's own Santy-worm framing — search-engine-driven mass exploitation against tens of thousands of forums — predicts exactly this burst-scan shape. Corroborated against the phpBB 3.3.17 release thread and Bleeping Computer's report which confirms the bug is trivially exploitable with a single unauthenticated request, making mass scanning the expected operator behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1595.002 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Search-engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) indexing public phpBB forum content including memberlist
  • Legitimate vulnerability scanners run by the asset owner (Nessus, Qualys, internal Aikido scans) probing the same phpBB endpoints
  • High-traffic single-user browsing where one human navigates memberlist → topic → login → ACP in normal session flow
  • Backup/mirror tools (wget, HTTrack) crawling the forum's full URL tree
  • CDN cache warming that hits a wide swathe of phpBB pages quickly
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !contains "Googlebot" and csUserAgent !contains "bingbot" and csUserAgent !contains "Pingdom" and csUserAgent !contains "DuckDuckBot" and csUserAgent !contains "DatadogSynthetics" and csUserAgent !contains "UptimeRobot" and csUserAgent !contains "Nessus" and csUserAgent !contains "Qualys"
| where cIP !in ("<approved-scanner-ip-1>", "<approved-scanner-ip-2>")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the source IP is external and not a known scanner / search-engine bot (rDNS check + ASN). Pull the full request stream from that cIP — were the responses 200 (likely exploit attempt) or 401/403 (failed scan)? Look for any 302 to an admin/session endpoint indicating a successful bypass. 2. Contain: if responses indicate successful auth bypass, block the source IP at WAF/edge, force-invalidate all phpBB sessions on the affected host, and rotate admin credentials. Confirm phpBB version is upgraded to 3.3.17 (or master for 4.x) — if not, take the forum into maintenance mode and patch before re-opening. 3. Hunt: pivot to all other phpBB instances in the estate and apply the same query; check for the same source IP touching multiple instances. Search outbound traffic from the phpBB host post-incident for web-shell C2 indicators (cobalt strike beacon shape, anomalous DNS).
let WindowMinutes = 5;
let PhpBbPaths = dynamic(["/memberlist.php", "/ucp.php", "/app.php/user/login", "/adm/index.php", "/viewtopic.php"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csUriStem in~ (PhpBbPaths) or csUriStem startswith "/user/oauth/authenticate/" or csUriStem startswith "/app.php/user/oauth/"
| summarize TotalRequests = count(),
            DistinctPaths = dcount(csUriStem),
            PathsHit = make_set(csUriStem, 10),
            UserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5),
            Methods = make_set(csMethod, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes * 1m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3 and TotalRequests >= 10
| extend MemberlistHit = tostring(PathsHit) contains "memberlist.php"
| extend AuthEndpointHit = tostring(PathsHit) contains "ucp.php" or tostring(PathsHit) contains "user/login" or tostring(PathsHit) contains "oauth/authenticate"
| where MemberlistHit and AuthEndpointHit
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:nginx.access OR source:apache.access OR source:iis) @http.url_details.path:(*/memberlist.php OR */ucp.php OR */app.php/user/login OR */user/oauth/authenticate/* OR */adm/index.php OR */app.php/user/oauth/*) -@http.useragent:(*Googlebot* OR *bingbot* OR *Pingdom* OR *DatadogSynthetics*)
WEB

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-29199")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-29199")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
